anchor_lock_design: operator secp lock; anchor lock continuity preserves operator control and requires its signature even after timeout
checkpoint_authorization: user key role 0 authorizes the deposit and operator key role 2 authorizes spending its anchor lock; the valid Groth16 proof authorizes the state transition
notes: The operator signs the checkpoint but disappears before the mature exit. A user-only mature exit is rejected by the operator secp lock; the same proof, timer, and payout succeed only after the operator signature is restored. This is an authorization boundary, not a timeout failure.

A separate child process fetched the committed checkpoint transaction through CKB RPC and reconstructed the force-exit proof from its published DA; no fixture/sequencer files were input to that reconstruction.
